summary: The skill entity page covers CanonicalSkill: instructions the model gets only when they matter, with a name, a one-line description the model reads when it may pick the skill, and macro-rendered text. A skill turns on always, when its triggers match, or while the model has it open, and its triggers are a lorebook entry's own fields matched by the lore engine's own matcher. A scene links skills by id in its prompting like tools and trackers, a turn reads them through its one library reader, and the ones on ride as one Skills block at the preset's skills marker, reserved by the budget so they are never dropped. The editor, the scene panel, opening skills and Kit editing them are not built yet.

sections.title: When it is on
sections.summary: A skill's when is always, mentioned or picked. Always puts it in the prompt every turn while linked. Mentioned uses a lorebook entry's own trigger fields, decoded by the lorebook's trigger decoder and matched by the lore engine's matchTrigger and selectiveLogicMatches over the newest scanDepth messages, the one being answered included, newest first, with regex triggers vetted; no triggers or a scan depth of 0 never match. Picked is on while the model has it open, and with closeWhenUnmentioned it closes when its triggers stop matching; opening and closing are not built yet, so a picked skill is never open today. Each verdict carries a plain sentence of why, returned on the assembly result.

sections.title: In a scene and in the prompt
sections.summary: A scene links skills by id in ChatPrompting.skills, in order with no duplicates, by the same rule as tools and trackers. A turn reads them through its one library reader, leaving out gone, unreadable and same-named skills. The skills that are on ride as one system message headed Skills, each name a heading over its rendered text, in the scene's order, and a blank one adds nothing. The block goes where the preset's skills marker stands with that block's role, otherwise after the leading system messages after the trackers' and storyboards' blocks. The budget reserves it like the library trackers' block, so history gives way and it is never dropped. The Tokens sheet labels it Skills.

sections.title: Not built yet
sections.summary: Not built yet: the Workbench editor from the approved skill wireframe, so a skill opens read-only in the Workbench for now; the scene's Skills panel and linking a skill from the scene; the picked skills' list that the model reads, with the open_skill and close_skill tools and the scene-state slot that keeps which skills are open, so a picked skill is never on today; a skill's own spot in the chat apart from the skills marker; and Kit making or editing a skill, since the kind has no Kit capabilities yet. Kit can already list, read, duplicate, export and delete skills through its generic piece tools, as for any kind.
